books.section: Topic 4.4 America on the World Stage, A. Trade, Diplomacy, and the Expansion of American Influence
Madison's Presidency and the War of 1812

stimulus.text:
The table shows the value of American foreign trade before and after the Embargo Act of 1807, which banned American ships from sailing to foreign ports.

| Year | Value of U.S. exports | Value of U.S. imports |
|------|----------------------|----------------------|
| 1807 | $108 million | $138 million |
| 1808 | $22 million | $56 million |
stimulus.source_note: Trade figures from U.S. trade statistics; export figures corroborated by Digital History, University of Houston.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note
stem: According to the table, the Embargo Act was followed by

options.text: a small rise in both exports and imports
options.misconception: Both columns fall sharply, so nothing rose.

options.text: a rise in exports and a fall in imports
options.misconception: Exports fell from $108 million to $22 million.

options.text: a sharp fall in both exports and imports
no change in the value of American trade
options.misconception: Exports fell by about four-fifths in a single year.

rationales.A: Both columns fall: exports from $108 million to $22 million, imports from $138 million to $56 million.
rationales.B: Exports did not rise. They fell from $108 million in 1807 to $22 million in 1808.
rationales.C: Both columns drop hard in one year. Exports fall by about four-fifths and imports by more than half.
rationales.D: Trade changed a great deal. Exports fell from $108 million to $22 million, and imports from $138 million to $56 million.
rationales.general:
1. Read the 1807 row. Exports were $108 million and imports $138 million.
2. Read the 1808 row. Exports were $22 million and imports $56 million.
3. Put it together. Both columns fell sharply in the year the embargo took hold.
Background: The Embargo Act banned American ships from sailing to foreign ports, so harbors went quiet.
Remember: when a table shows before and after, compare the same column across the two rows.
